correctness.rationale: Different word permutations differ at some initial point, and an accepting singleton then separates the two endpoints; identical word permutations cannot be separated. Write H_m for the normal subgroup generated by m-th powers. Two sets of powers commute pairwise exactly when their generated subgroups centralize each other. For S_3 the possible H_m are S_3, A_3 and 1; the two nontrivial choices centralize one another only when both are A_3. For S_4 the choices are S_4 for odd m, A_4 for even m not divisible by 3, V_4 for m≡6 mod 12, and 1 otherwise. Conjugation by a 3-cycle is nontrivial on V_4, so only the V_4/V_4 nontrivial pair centralizes. S_1 and S_2 are abelian. For d≥5, E_d is the exponent; if it does not divide m, a cycle witnesses a nontrivial power. Odd m retains all transpositions and even m gives a nontrivial normal subgroup of the simple A_d. Both nontrivial possibilities therefore contain the same nonabelian A_d. This proves the exact lower and upper thresholds, and the LCM increases precisely at a prime power, giving the stated corollary for r=s=E_N, N≥4. A separate permutation enumeration covered every residue pair in S_3 and S_4 (36 and 144 pairs, respectively) and agreed with the criteria.
residual_risks: Residue enumeration checks only degrees 3 and 4. The theorem is about complete permutation automata, not unrestricted deterministic automata.

originality.rationale: Two distinct published records directly cover the exact two-run classification; one states the degree-by-degree predicate and gives stronger shortest-length and minimizer results. Both catalogue dates are later than the frozen record’s and do not establish that the frozen authors were anticipated, nor do they establish independent provenance. The failure is affirmative equivalent coverage in the audited corpus, not a historical priority ruling and not an inference from inaccessible literature.
residual_risks: No inference about historical priority from catalogue dating or textual overlap. The full Karpova–Shur and Gimadeev–Vyalyi scopes remain unresolved; these access limits are not the basis for failure.
